label: Double-hung Sash Window
volunteer_identification_guide: Two counterbalanced vertically sliding glazed sashes within boxed timber frame; sashes held by cords, pulleys, and lead weights.

label: Casement Window (Hinged Side)
volunteer_identification_guide: Glazed timber frame hinged at side swinging outwards or inwards; secured by casement stay and fastener.

label: Sliding Horizontal Window
volunteer_identification_guide: Glazed panels sliding horizontally along timber tracks; frequent in vernacular sheds and enclosed verandahs.

label: Fixed Pane Window
volunteer_identification_guide: Stationary glass pane glazed directly into timber frame without operating mechanism.

label: Timber Shutter Only (Unglazed)
volunteer_identification_guide: Hinged solid timber or battened shutter closing an open aperture; typical of remote huts, meat houses, and shearing sheds.

label: Timber or Glass Louvre
volunteer_identification_guide: Horizontal angled slats admitting airflow while blocking direct sunlight or rain; common in dairies and verandahs.

label: 12-Pane Sash (6 over 6)
volunteer_identification_guide: Six small glass panes per sash divided by fine timber glazing bars; standard Colonial and early Victorian configuration before large sheet cylinder glass became economical.

label: 6-Pane Sash (3 over 3)
volunteer_identification_guide: Three panes per sash; transitional format.

label: 4-Pane Sash (2 over 2)
volunteer_identification_guide: Two panes per sash separated by central vertical glazing bar; dominant mid-to-late Victorian style.

label: 2-Pane Sash (1 over 1)
volunteer_identification_guide: Single large sheet of plate/sheet glass per sash without intermediate glazing bars; horn mouldings on lower sash stiles.

label: Single Large Sheet Pane
volunteer_identification_guide: Uninterrupted sheet of plate or float glass.

label: Ledged & Braced Door
volunteer_identification_guide: Vertical tongue-and-groove or plain boards stiffened by horizontal ledges and diagonal timber braces on rear; standard vernacular and service door.

label: 4-Panel Door (Low-Waisted Victorian)
volunteer_identification_guide: Four recessed timber panels (two tall upper, two short lower) separated by mid-rail positioned low; quintessential Victorian interior door.

label: 6-Panel Door (Colonial / Georgian)
volunteer_identification_guide: Six recessed moulded timber panels arranged in 3 vertical pairs; diagnostic Georgian and early Colonial domestic joinery.

label: High-waisted Panelled Door
volunteer_identification_guide: Mid-rail positioned high (above center) with long vertical lower panels; diagnostic Federation, Edwardian, and Interwar joinery.

label: French Doors (Pair Glazed)
volunteer_identification_guide: Pair of narrow glazed casement doors opening out onto verandah, providing light, ventilation, and garden access.

label: Half-Door / Stable Door (Dutch Door)
volunteer_identification_guide: Horizontally split door where top and bottom leaves open independently; traditional for stables and tack rooms.

label: Large Sliding Shed Door (Top Track)
volunteer_identification_guide: Heavy timber or CGI clad door suspended on overhead iron rollers and track; standard for woolshed wool rooms and wagon entrances.

label: Rim Lock (Surface-mounted Iron Box)
volunteer_identification_guide: Cast or wrought iron box lock mounted directly onto interior surface of door leaf; brass drop handle and large iron keyhole.

label: Mortise Lock (Internal Recess)
volunteer_identification_guide: Lock mechanism fitted into pocket mortised inside the thickness of the door stile; brass or ceramic doorknob.

label: Norfolk / Suffolk Thumb Latch
volunteer_identification_guide: Wrought or cast-iron lift latch operated by exterior thumb-lever passing through slot in door.

label: Timber Drop-Bar / Slip Rail
volunteer_identification_guide: Heavy wooden bar resting in wrought-iron brackets across interior of door leaf for internal security in sheds and outbuildings.

label: T-Hinges / Strap Hinges (Surface)
volunteer_identification_guide: Long wrought-iron strap fastened across door ledges pivoting on gudgeon pin or frame plate; supports heavy timber doors.

label: Butt Hinges (Cast Iron / Steel)
volunteer_identification_guide: Flanged rectangular hinge mortised flush into door stile and jamb.
